meta.scope: Kush to 1956 plus Torit 1955; major wars and decisive battles only
meta.coords: db/cities.json entries only; precision region = no lat/lon
meta.quote_note: cites[].quote = verbatim passage from the cited page (box copy; OCR letter-spacing and line-break hyphens removed; GHA macrons restored where OCR rendered them as umlauts). No quote = none taken.

battles.name_ar: حملة تحتمس الأول على كرمة [يحتاج تحقق]
battles.outcome_en: Egyptian victory; the kingdom of Kerma was defeated (c.1500 BCE, shortly before)
battles.label: Thutmose I's campaign against Kerma 150 BCE

cites.quote: Sous le règne suivant, celui de Thoutmosis Ier, l’expédition contre Koush, lancée dès l’an 2 (à placer sans doute peu avant 1 500 av. J.‑C.), prit une toute autre ampleur et porta un coup sévère au royaume de Kerma.

battles.decisive_note: No cited page calls it decisive.

battles.name_en: Psamtik II's expedition against Napatan Kush (Pnoubs/Kerma)
battles.name_ar: حملة بسماتيك الثاني على مملكة نبتة (بنوبس/كرمة) [يحتاج تحقق]
battles.outcome_en: Egyptian expedition reached Pnoubs/Kerma and ravaged the country
battles.label: Psamtik II's expedition against Napatan Kush (Pnoubs/Kerma) 593 BCE

cites.quote: un second corps expéditionnaire remonta le Nil jusqu’à Pnoubs/Kerma où ils ravagèrent le pays et massacrèrent les Nubiens

battles.decisive_note: No cited page calls it decisive.

battles.name_en: Petronius's expedition and capture of Napata
battles.name_ar: حملة بترونيوس والاستيلاء على نبتة [يحتاج تحقق]
battles.outcome_en: Roman force captured Napata; a garrison was placed at Primis (Qasr Ibrim)
battles.label: Petronius's expedition and capture of Napata 23 BCE
battles.significance_en: Petronius's counter-campaign reached Napata after Meroitic forces took Syene, Elephantine and Philae (GHA II p.290; SFDAS pp.243–244).

cites.quote: the prefect of Roman Egypt, Petronius, mounted a punitive expedition and captured Napata in —23. A permanent garrison was established by the Romans at Primis (Qasr Ibrim), which held off the Meroites.

battles.decisive_note: No cited page calls it decisive.

battles.name_en: Ezana of Aksum's campaign against the Kushites and Noba
battles.name_ar: حملة عيزانا ملك أكسوم على الكوشيين والنوبة [يحتاج تحقق]
battles.outcome_en: Aksumite campaign recorded in Ezana's inscriptions; the Meroitic state disappeared between 330 and 350 CE
battles.label: Ezana of Aksum's campaign against the Kushites and Noba 330
battles.significance_en: Ezana's Ge'ez inscription DAE 11 records his war against the Noba and the Kasu at the Nile–Atbara confluence (SFDAS pp.325–326).

cites.quote: Le texte décrit une région où le pouvoir central méroïtique n’existe déjà plus et qui est désormais aux mains des Noubas, à l’exception de quelques enclaves encore tenues par les Kasu, c’est-à-dire les Koushites, contre qui Ézana engage également un combat victorieux.

battles.decisive_note: No cited page calls it decisive.

battles.name_ar: الحملة العربية الأولى على المقرة [يحتاج تحقق]
battles.outcome_en: Nubian counter-offensive turned back the Arab army
battles.label: First Arab campaign against Makuria 642

cites.quote: Vers 642, une armée musulmane menée par Abdallah Abou Sarh, futur gouverneur de l’Égypte, est à la frontière de Makouria et attaque le pays. Mais la contre-offensive des Nubiens désoriente les Arabes, qui subissent de lourdes pertes.

battles.decisive_note: No cited page calls it decisive.

battles.name_en: Siege of Dongola and the Baqt treaty
battles.outcome_en: Expedition launched 651 besieged Dongola; ended in a truce and the Baqt treaty (652), which kept Makuria independent
battles.label: Siege of Dongola and the Baqt treaty 652

cites.quote: En 651 Abdallah Abou Sarh, qui avait succédé à Amr Ibn al-‘As comme gouverneur d’Égypte, lança une seconde expédition contre Makouria avec une forte armée. Cette fois, il atteignit sans difficulté la capitale, Dongola, et en fit le siège en usant de catapultes

battles.decisive_note: No cited page calls it decisive.

battles.outcome_en: Funj victory; the Abdallabi king became a Funj vassal
battles.label: Arbaji 1504
battles.significance_en: The Funj victory made the Abdallabi king a Funj vassal (GHA V ch.7 p.173).

cites.quote: At Arbadji, in 1504, the Fundj defeated the 'Abdallabi and their king was reduced to the position of vassal.

battles.decisive_note: No cited page calls it decisive.

battles.name_en: Funj campaign against the Musabba'at in Kordofan
battles.name_ar: حملة الفونج على المسبعات في كردفان [يحتاج تحقق]
battles.outcome_en: Decisive Funj victory after initial setbacks; Abu Likaylik ruled Kordofan as viceroy
battles.label: Funj campaign against the Musabba'at in Kordofan 1747

cites.quote: After initial setbacks, the Fundj army, under the command of Muhammad Abu Likaylik, won a decisive victory in 1747.

battles.decisive_note: GHA V ch.7 p.178 calls it a 'decisive victory'.

battles.outcome_en: Mahdist victory; a turning point of the Mahdist revolution
battles.label: Shaykan 1883

cites.quote: The Ansār completely annihilated their enemy at Shaykān's forest in the neighbourhood of al-'Obeid.

battles.decisive_note: GHA VII ch.4 p.76 calls it a 'turning-point', not decisive; left false.

battles.outcome_en: Mahdist forces took the town after a long siege, ending Turco-Egyptian rule
battles.label: Fall of Khartoum 1885

cites.quote: attacked the town, killed Gordon on 26 January 1885, and put an end to Turco-Egyptian rule in the Sudan.

battles.decisive_note: No cited page calls it decisive.

battles.outcome_en: Mahdist invasion of Egypt was defeated
battles.label: Toski 1889

cites.quote: Under the leadership of 'Abd al-Raḥmān al-Nudjūmī, the Mahdist forces invaded Egypt, but they were defeated at the battle of Tushki in 1889.

battles.decisive_note: No cited page calls it decisive.

battles.outcome_en: Emperor mortally wounded at the close of the battle; his army dispersed
battles.label: Gallabat (Matamma) 1889

cites.quote: The emperor hastened to Matamma to resist them, but at the close of a victorious battle on 10 March 1889, was mortally wounded by a stray bullet. News of his death caused his army to disintegrate.

battles.decisive_note: No cited page calls it decisive.

battles.outcome_en: Anglo-Egyptian victory; Mahmud Ahmad captured
battles.label: the Atbara 1898

cites.quote: Commanded by Emir Maḥmūd Aḥmad, the Ansār tried unsuccessfully to repel the enemy attack at the battle of Atbara on 8 April 1898.

battles.decisive_note: Churchill, River War I p.449: 'the battle of the Atbara had been decisive'.

battles.outcome_en: Anglo-Egyptian victory; the Khalifa withdrew to Kordofan
battles.label: Karari (Omdurman) 1898

cites.quote: the Sudanese fought the enemy with magnificent courage at the battle of Karari on 2 September 1898. Once again they were defeated by superior armaments.

battles.decisive_note: Churchill, River War I p.113: the Dervish empire 'ended abruptly … in the battle of Omdurman'; p.132 'the Dervish Empire was doomed to be shattered' on the Kerreri plain.

battles.outcome_en: The Khalifa died on the field; collapse of the Mahdist state
battles.label: Umm Diwaykarat 1899

cites.quote: was finally defeated at the battle of Umm Diwaykrāt on 24 November 1899. After the battle, the Khalīfa was found dead upon his sheepskin prayer-rug

battles.decisive_note: GHA VII ch.4 p.78: battle marked the collapse of the Mahdist state.

battles.outcome_en: Ali Dinar defeated and killed; Darfur incorporated into Sudan
battles.label: Defeat of Sultan Ali Dinar 1916

cites.quote: Not until February 1916 was he defeated and killed in battle and Dārfūr fully incorporated into Sudan.

battles.decisive_note: No cited page calls it decisive.

battles.outcome_en: Mutineers soon surrendered; disorder spread in the south
battles.label: Torit mutiny (Equatoria Corps revolt) 1955
battles.significance_en: The Torit mutiny of August 1955 is the start point of the first civil war (GHA VIII p.149).

cites.quote: in August 1955 the Equatoria Corps of the Sudanese army revolted against the gradual take-over of the administration and command posts by the northerners. Although the mutineers soon surrendered, disorder had by that time spread through the southern provinces

battles.decisive_note: No cited page calls it decisive.

battles.region: Memphis, Lower Egypt (no gazetteer coordinate registered)
battles.outcome_en: Piye took Memphis and received the submission of the Delta rulers (SFDAS p.138).
battles.significance_en: The Victory Stela of Piye, a 159-line granite text, narrates the campaign of year 21 (SFDAS p.137). After Hermopolis his army moved on Memphis, where the enemy chiefs had entrenched (SFDAS p.138).
battles.id_note: Requested id memphis--728 not used: no registered page gives 728; GHA II p.106 gives 'about −720'.

cites.quote: Mais Piankhy fait saisir tous les bateaux disponibles et envoie ses soldats éperonner les murs en un assaut unique, forçant ainsi les défenses de l’ennemi. La ville est prise, avec un butin considérable.

battles.label: Piye's capture of Memphis 720 BCE
battles.decisive_note: No cited page calls it decisive.

battles.outcome_en: Mamluk army reached Dongola and set Shekanda on the throne under heavy tribute (SFDAS p.419).
battles.significance_en: Baybars's army invaded Nubia and reached Dongola in 1276. It installed King Shekanda with a heavy tribute and ceded whole provinces to Mamluk control (SFDAS p.419).

cites.quote: Son armée envahit la Nubie et poussa jusqu’à Dongola en 1276, où elle rétablit sur le trône le roi Shékanda, lui imposant toutefois un lourd tribut et la cession de provinces entières au pouvoir mamelouk.

battles.label: Mamluk expedition to Dongola 1276
battles.decisive_note: No cited page calls it decisive.

battles.name_ar: الاستيلاء العثماني على قصر إبريم [يحتاج تحقق]
battles.outcome_en: Ottoman forts built at Aswan, Qasr Ibrim and Sai; Qasr Ibrim became the provincial capital (SFDAS pp.423–424).
battles.significance_en: Özdemir Pasha took Qasr Ibrim and left Bosnian battalions to build forts at Aswan, Qasr Ibrim and Sai. The province, with Qasr Ibrim as capital, lasted until Napoleon's invasion of Egypt (SFDAS pp.423–424).

cites.quote: Celui-ci partit avec une armée de 40 000 hommes vers le Soudan, où il s’empara de Qasr Ibrim.

battles.label: Ottoman capture of Qasr Ibrim 1560
battles.decisive_note: No cited page calls it decisive.

battles.region: Near Tokar, Red Sea littoral, just north of the later fort (Gleichen V1 p.15)
battles.outcome_en: Fought 29 February 1884 during the British expedition to relieve Tokar (Wingate p.117).
battles.significance_en: A 4,000-strong British expedition under Graham landed at Suakin to relieve Tokar and fought at El Teb on 29 February 1884 (Wingate p.117). Gleichen places the battlefield just north of the Tokar fort (V1 p.15).

cites.quote: The battle of El Teb, fought on the 29th February, showed hard hand-to-hand fighting.

battles.label: El Teb 1884
battles.decisive_note: No cited page calls it decisive.

battles.outcome_en: Graham's force drove the Mahdist forces into the hills (Wingate p.118).
battles.significance_en: On 13 March 1884 Graham met a larger Mahdist force at Tamai after a hard fight (Wingate pp.117–118). An attempt to open the Suakin–Berber road to Gordon was then considered (Wingate p.118).
battles.page_note: Wingate p.118 OCR page label unverified; RIVERWAR1899_V1 index i.78.

cites.quote: on the 13th March, Graham caught the Arabs in still greater force, 12,000 according to careful estimate, and, after a fierce and obstinate fight at Tamai, he killed 2000 and brushed the remainder into the hills.

battles.label: Tamai 1884
battles.decisive_note: No cited page calls it decisive.

battles.region: Bayuda desert, on the Korti–Metemma route
battles.outcome_en: The British advanced guard defeated the combined Mahdist force (Slatin p.204).
battles.significance_en: Wingate calls the battle of 17 January 1885 'unlooked-for but decisive' (p.172). Slatin records that the force under Musa Wad Helu was defeated at Abu Teleh (Abu Klea) (p.204).
battles.decisive_note: Wingate 1891 p.172: 'the unlooked-for but decisive battle of Abu Klea'.

cites.quote: the English advanced guard had met the combined force of Barabra, Jaalin, Degheim, and Kenana, under Musa Wad Helu, at Abu Teleh (Abu Klea), and had utterly defeated them

battles.label: Abu Klea 1885

battles.region: Ginnis and Kosheh, east bank of the Nile, Dongola frontier
battles.outcome_en: Mahdist advance sustained a severe repulse (River War I p.157).
battles.significance_en: On the last day but one of 1885 the Mahdists pressing north met a severe repulse at Ginnis under Stephenson (River War I p.157). It was the first action of the reformed Egyptian troops (River War I p.155).

cites.quote: at Ginniss, on the last day but one of the year, they sustained a severe repulse at the hands of Sir Frederick Stephenson.

battles.label: Ginnis 1885
battles.decisive_note: No cited page calls it decisive.

battles.outcome_en: Italians advanced from Agordat and captured Kassala; occupation provisionally recognised by Egypt (River War I p.356).
battles.significance_en: After a Mahdist attack on Agordat in 1893, the Italians under Baratieri advanced the next year and captured Kassala (River War I pp.355–356). Egypt recognised the occupation provisionally, without prejudice to her rights (p.356).
battles.date_note: Year derived from 'in 1893 … in the next year' (River War I pp.355–356).

cites.quote: the Italians under General Baratieri advanced from Agordat and captured Kassala. The occupation was provisionally recognised by Egypt without prejudice to her sovereign rights

battles.label: Italian capture of Kassala 1894
battles.decisive_note: No cited page calls it decisive.

battles.region: Firket, Nile above Akasha, Dongola province
battles.outcome_en: Capture of Firket village and pursuit (River War I p.220, chapter summary).
battles.significance_en: The action of 7 June 1896 opened the Dongola expedition authorised in March 1896 (River War I pp.181, 220). The Mahdist force under Emir Hammuda had held Firket since late 1895 (p.220).

cites.quote: FIRKET June 7, 1896. [...] Firket village — The deployment MacDonald's brigade — Capture of the village — The pursuit

battles.label: Firket (Ferkeh) 1896
battles.decisive_note: No cited page calls it decisive.
